messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — CI perf alert just flagged a 18% p95 latency regression downstream of attention kernel routing. Seen on nightly when serving seq=1024/2048 tails.
aj: Oof. Any obvious diff between flashattn vs paged path?
sara: I skimmed a trace: lots of small kernels executed on the flash path, but on some batches it falls back to paged and runtime is thrashing between kernels. looks like kernel chooser oscillation.
maria: Exact. Snapshot from the console: route decision rate jumps at t=12:41 and we get a KV cache cold miss spike. Attn pick logs: `choosers: [flashattn, flashpaged, paged]` alternating.
leo: Can you paste the profiler snippet? nvprof / Nsight output would help.
perf-bot: perf-regression: alert triggered for service=redwood-serving, model=vicuna-13b, metric=p95_latency, delta=+18% (12:40–12:55 UTC)
sara: Pasted a lean profile (trimmed):
```
Time(ms)  Kernel             Calls  Avg
0.84      flash_attn_fwd      432    1.94
1.32      flash_paged_fwd     78     16.90
0.21      generic_attn_fwd    12     17.50
```
Notice flash_paged has much higher avg due to a couple of heavy batches (seq=2048 + batch=8).
maria: Repro script I used:
```
./run_perf.sh --model vicuna-13b --seq 2048 --batch 8 --profile nv
```
Got baseline (prev commit abc123): p95=96ms, current (def456): p95=113ms.
aj: Sounds like chooser heuristic mispredicts when KV cache is partially warm. Batch coalescer occasionally merges short and long sequences into the same request bundle. We should see degraded locality and kernel warmup thrash.
leo: I ran a narrow bisect quickly between abc123..def456 and narrowed to commit def200 which changed batching heuristic: "coalesce_threshold lowered to 0.3". That seems suspicious.
sara: Lower threshold means coalescer more aggressively mixes sequences. For variable-length workloads that can land a 2k seq in a batch with many <128 seqs — KV cache thrash + different kernel choice per request causes context switches.
maria: Quick experiment: force-route all to flash_paged to measure stable baseline (bypass chooser). Command:
```
REDWOOD_FORCE_ATTENTION=flash_paged ./run_perf.sh --seq 2048 --batch 8
```
Result: p95=108ms (better than 113ms but slightly worse than baseline). When forcing flashattn: p95=100ms. So the oscillation is the culprit.
aj: Good. Two actionable ideas: 1) revert coalesce_threshold change or 2) add coalescer awareness of max-seq in bundle so we don't mix long+short. Also update chooser to consider recent kernel latency variance, not just expected throughput.
leo: I sketched a small patch to coalescer: if max_seq_in_window / median_seq > 8 then don't coalesce across sizes. Quick microbench looks promising (~6% p95 improvement on mix workload).
sara: Also let's add a short TTL-based sticky kernel selection: once a kernel chosen for a model/seq bucket, prefer it for N seconds unless throughput drops. That reduces oscillation.
maria: Can someone open a PR with the revert + targeted heuristic? I'll run longer nightly with A/B.
aj: I'll file one and include the bisect notes + commands + perf bot graphs.
leo: PR link incoming: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/4821 — includes microbench numbers and a small unit test that simulates mixed-length bursts.
perf-bot: perf-check: started nightly A/B for PR 4821 vs main — ETA 3h.
sara: Nice. For postmortem notes: root cause = aggressive coalescer change + chooser lacking variance signal + KV cache cold/warm interplay. Mitigations = revert/guard + sticky chooser + coalescer size-aware rule + add more synthetic mixed-length perf tests.
maria: Agreed. I'll add a probe to the console that surfaces "coalesce mix ratio" and "chooser flip rate" so we can detect regressions earlier. :thumbsup:
aj: Thanks team — assign owners: maria (observability probe), leo (coalescer patch), sara (sticky chooser), aj (PR + rollout plan).
leo: I'll also drop a short runbook snippet for oncall: if p95 jumps and chooser flip_rate > 2/min, temporarily set REDWOOD_FORCE_ATTENTION=flashattn until rollback/patch.
maria: Perfect. Closing loop here. Will post results when perf-bot finishes.
